newsitem.title: SWEDEN: MoDo says hard to see lower pulp stocks.
newsitem.headline: MoDo says hard to see lower pulp stocks.

text.p: Head of Swedish forestry company MoDo, Bengt Pettersson, said on Thursday it was hard to see pulp producers' stocks in North America and Scandinavia (NorScan) falling significantly from current levels.
"NorScan stocks are an important signal, but a change of about 100,000 tonnes has no real significance. A stock level of about 1.5 to 1.6 million tonnes is low," Pettersson told a news conference.
"I have trouble seeing stocks falling much lower than that."
According to market sources, NorScan stock levels, excluding Norway, increased by 126,000 tonnes in July.
This would mean stock levels are now 1.65 million tonnes.
Pettersson said the announced rises in pulp prices can go through but he could not say when they would happen.
"It is difficult to say when they will go through. First we will negotiate with clients and August is usually a weaker month on the ground of the holidays on the continent," he said.
Some producers have already announced plans to lift the price for long fibre pulp to $610 a tonne and for short fibre pulp to 510 ECU a tonne.
